contentBlocks.text: This week you took the area model from 2-digit numbers all the way to 2-digit-by-2-digit multiplication and real word problems. Let's review it all.

Quick review: the area model breaks any number into place-value pieces (hundreds, tens, ones), multiplies each piece separately, then adds the results together. This worked for 2-digit x 1-digit (Day 1), 3-digit x 1-digit (Day 2), and 2-digit x 2-digit with four partial products (Day 3) — and you applied it to real word problems (Day 4). Solve one of each type below to show you've got all four.
Excellent work this week — you now have a real, reliable method for multiplying any size of number, and you know how to apply it to real-world problems.

objectives: Correctly apply the area model to 2-digit x 1-digit, 3-digit x 1-digit, and 2-digit x 2-digit multiplication
Solve a real-world word problem using multi-digit multiplication
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Complete the cumulative review worksheet, one problem of each type from the week.
3. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
4. Celebrate finishing the first full week of this unit — this same area-model technique will keep extending to even bigger numbers in future units.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to draw the area-model grid for every problem, even the simplest one, as a supportive habit
Ready for more: ask them to solve a 3-digit x 2-digit problem (6 partial products) to see the pattern extend further
This is a good checkpoint to note which day's problem type needs the most re-teaching before moving to next week's unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. 42 x 6 = 252. 2. 341 x 4 = 1,364. 3. 27 x 13 = 351. 4. A shelf holds 16 boxes with 9 books in each box — how many books? 16 x 9 = 144 books.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates the week's Common Core 4.NBT.5 multiplication progression (2-digit through 2x2-digit, plus word-problem application) before the unit moves to a new topic, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established across this session.
